purpose: Mobocertinib is used to treat a specific type of non-small cell lung cancer in adults whose cancer has spread and is caused by a certain genetic change called an EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation. It is used when your cancer has gotten worse after trying at least one other chemotherapy treatment. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Think of cancer cells as having a faulty "on switch" that tells them to grow out of control. Mobocertinib works by blocking that specific faulty switch — a protein called EGFR with an exon 20 insertion mutation — so cancer cells get the signal to stop growing. This makes it a targeted therapy, meaning it is designed to go after the specific change driving your cancer rather than attacking all cells in your body.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea (very common and can be severe), nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, dry or itchy skin, rash, mouth sores, decreased appetite, fatigue, and low levels of certain nutrients like sodium or magnesium in your blood.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems, including a change in heart rhythm called QTc prolongation, which can be life-threatening — your doctor will monitor your heart with regular EKGs. It can also cause serious lung inflammation (called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis), which can be fatal. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after. Avoid grapefruit and certain other medicines that can interact with it.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 160 mg (four 40 mg capsules) taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose as scheduled — do not double up.
